text:
marta: FYI handing off the customer-managed throttling doc for Private/VPC installs. Need API+Console + ops agreement before docs go live.
kevin: thanks — do we have a quick decision on enforcement point? ingress proxy vs runtime? :thinking_face:
noor: leaning proxy for predictable per-tenant shaping, runtime can be secondary for per-key nuance. proxy -> reject vs runtime -> soft-throttle.
adele: runtime has the KV-cache awareness so it can do burst-return behavior better (replenish tokens on idle). but it means every host needs the policy.
sam: security note: any customer-managed policy upload must be signed and audited. we can't allow arbitrary rate overrides without identity + KMS signing.
marta: agreed. proposal: policy authored by tenant ops, signed with customer's key, pushed to S3-style bucket, and distributed via controller with signature verification. UI shows last-applied sig + audit id.
kevin: that sounds heavy for smaller customers. can we support two modes: managed (redwood-controlled policy) or delegated (customer-managed signed policy)? default = managed.
noor: yep. managed -> control plane serves policies. delegated -> controller pulls from customer endpoint or bucket. we already have awork for pulling TLS-mutual endpoints.
adele: UX question: in Console, do we let customers 'simulate' a policy before applying? would help avoid accidental lockouts.
marta: yes — sandbox apply w/ dry-run logs and per-route token counters displayed.
kevin: moving to config specifics — propose JSON schema (example):
```json
{
  "policy_version": "2026-01",
  "tenant_id": "t-1234",
  "rules": [
    {"key": "per_org", "rate": "50r/s", "burst": 200},
    {"key": "api_key", "rate": "10r/s", "burst": 50}
  ],
  "fail_mode": "closed",
  "signature": "base64sig..."
}
```
noor: minor nit: use tokens/sec and burst_tokens to avoid ambiguous units. also add "scope": "global|route|model".
sam: plus metadata: author, signed_at, signer_key_id, and audit_url.
marta: good. add observability hooks: per-policy counters, last_evaluated_ts, enforcement_node. console should link to traces when a deny occurs.
kevin: enforcement semantics: proxy enforces per_org global shaping; runtime enforces per_key/kvcached burst adjustments. fallback rules: if signature invalid -> reject update; if controller can't reach bucket -> continue using last-known policy; if no policy -> default to managed with conservative limits.
adele: implement token-bucket with refill rate computed per-window, expose current tokens in /metrics. example prometheus metric: `redwood_throttle_tokens{tenant=\"t-1234\",scope=\"api_key\"} 42`
noor: ops: we need a rolling restart plan for controller when a delegated-policy is added — avoid simultaneous expiry leading to fail-closed for many tenants. prefer sidecar prefetch + warm cache.
marta: action items: @kevin draft public API for policy upload + verify flow; @adele runtime changes for token expose + dry-run; @noor rollout plan + controller resilience tests; @sam write signing/keys checklist. I can centralize into an RFC by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:
kevin: on it. will sketch endpoints `/v1/private/policies/{tenant}` (PUT signed blob) and `/v1/private/policies/{tenant}/simulate` (POST).
noor: adding a test matrix: network partition, bad signature, expired signature, large policy, rollback. I'll write e2e tests.
sam: I'll draft KMS integration note and key rotation impacts.
adele: quick Q — do we want per-route burst overrides or only per-tenant/per-key? small customers want route-level throttles.
marta: allow per-route but UI hides complexity unless advanced mode toggled. default policy precedence: route > api_key > org.
deploy-bot: deploy queued for branch `private-throttle-rfc` — tests pending. (CI: 4/8 passed)
kevin: thanks everyone. will ping when RFC is merged. :eyes:
